title: United States begins Operation Rough Rider air campaign against the Houthis
body:
On 15 March 2025 the United States began a sustained air campaign against Houthi targets in Yemen, known as Operation Rough Rider. President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that the Houthis were waging "piracy, violence, and terrorism" and that "your time is up, and your attacks must stop, starting today." Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Houthi attacks would not be tolerated and that Iran was "on notice." At least 40 air raids were reported on the first day, with targets including radar, air defences, launch sites, headquarters, weapons storage and Sanaa International Airport.

Casualty figures differ by source. The Houthi health ministry said at least 53 people were killed on the first day. The Pentagon's assessment was 153 civilians killed and 243 wounded. Airwars counted 224 civilians killed, and the Houthis claimed 123 killed and 247 wounded between 15 March and 15 April. The Houthis claimed missile and drone attacks on the USS Harry S. Truman on 16 March, and a US official said 11 drones were shot down and one missile failed in flight. The United States lost two F/A-18 Super Hornets and seven MQ-9 Reaper drones during the campaign.

Before the campaign, the Houthis had attacked more than 190 ships since November 2023, sinking two, seizing one and killing at least four seafarers. The operation ended on 6 May 2025, when Trump declared the strikes over under an Oman-brokered ceasefire with the Houthis.
